Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Daraqutni in al-Afrad, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, and al-Khatib in his History narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say on the pulpit: "It occurred to the soul of Musa: Does Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sleep? So Allah sent to him an angel, who kept him awake for three nights, and gave him two flasks, one in each hand, and commanded him to guard them. He began to sleep, and his hands almost met, then he would wake and hold one back over the other, until he slept a single sleep, and his hands jerked and the two flasks broke." He said: "Allah struck for him a parable: if Allah, Blessed and Exalted, were to sleep, the heavens and the earth would not remain held together."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Salam that Musa said: "O Jibril, does your Lord sleep?" and he mentioned something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from his father, that Musa (said), and he mentioned something similar.

al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim (who authenticated it) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Indeed, the dung beetle is almost punished in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature﴾ (the verse).

Then, after He (glory be to Him) had finished speaking of the reward of His righteous servants, He mentioned the recompense of His wicked servants, saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell. They will not be decreed a death so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them.﴾ That is, no decree of death will be issued against them so that they might die and be at rest from the punishment. ﴿Nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾ — rather, ﴿every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment﴾ [an-Nisa: 56]. This verse is like His (glory be to Him) saying: ﴿Neither will he die therein nor live﴾ [Ta-Ha: 74]. The majority of readers read "fa-yamutu" (so that they die) in the accusative, as a response to the negation. ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar and al-Hasan read it with the nun retained (fa-yamutuna).

Al-Mazini said: it is in conjunction with "yuqda" (be decreed).

Ibn ʿAtiyya said: it is a weak reading, and there is no basis for this weakening; rather it is like His saying: ﴿nor will they be permitted, so that they may make excuses﴾ [al-Mursalat: 36]. ﴿Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ — that is, like that dreadful recompense, We recompense everyone who is extreme in disbelief. Abu ʿAmr read "yujza" in the passive voice.

﴿And they will cry out therein﴾ — from as-sarakh (al-sarakh), which is shouting, that is: they will call for help in the Fire, raising their voices. As-sarikh (al-sarikh) is the one who seeks help, and from this is the saying of the poet:

"When a frightened crier came to us, the shouting was for him a beating of the tambourine-skins."

﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteous deeds, other than what we used to do﴾ — that is, while they are therein crying out, they say: "Our Lord, etc."

Muqatil said: it is that they call out: "Our Lord, bring us out, we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do," from shirk and sins, so that we make faith in place of what we were upon of disbelief, and obedience in place of disobedience. The accusative of "salihan" is because it is an adjective of a deleted verbal noun, i.e., a righteous deed, or an adjective of a deleted noun, i.e., we will do something righteous.

It has been said: the addition of "other than what we used to do" is for regret over what they did of non-righteous deeds, along with their admission that their deeds in the world were not righteous. So God (glory be to Him) answers them with His saying: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would take heed might take heed therein?﴾ The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach, and the waw is for conjunction with an assumed element, as in its similar cases. "Ma" is an indefinite qualified noun, i.e., Did We not give you a lifespan in which whoever would be mindful could be mindful?

It was said: it is sixty years. It was said: forty. It was said: eighteen years. A group of the Companions said the first, al-Hasan and Masruq and others the second, and ʿAta' and Qatada the third.

al-Aʿmash read "ma yadhdhakkaru" with idgham (assimilation). ﴿And the warner came to you﴾. al-Wahidi said: most of the exegetes said: he is the Prophet (ﷺ).

ʿIkrima, Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna, Waki', al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl, al-Farra', and Ibn Jarir said: he is white hair (ash-shayb), and the meaning on this view is: Did We not give you life until you grew gray? It was said: he is the Qur'an. It was said: fever.

al-Azhari said: its meaning is that fever is the messenger of death, as it were, it signals its arrival and warns of its coming. White hair is also a warner, because it comes at the age of middle years, and it is a sign of leaving the age of youth, which is the age of play and amusement. It was said: he is the death of family and relatives. It was said: he is the perfection of intellect. It was said: puberty. ﴿So taste, for the wrongdoers have no helper﴾ — that is: taste the punishment of Hell, because you did not take heed and were not admonished; so you have no helper who would prevent you from the punishment of God or stand between you and it.

Muqatil said: "Taste the punishment; the polytheists have no preventer who would prevent them."

﴿Indeed, God knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾. The majority read "ʿalim" (knower) as idafa to "ghayb" (unseen). Jinah ibn Hubaysh read it with tanwin and the accusative "ghaybang" (ghaiban).

The meaning: He knows everything, and among that are deeds which are not hidden from Him; not one of them is concealed. So if He returned you to the world, you would not do righteous deeds, as He (glory be to Him) said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would revert to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾ — this is a justification of what precedes it, for when He knows the hidden thoughts within the breasts, which are the most hidden of all things, He knows what is above them a fortiori. It was said: this sentence explains the first sentence.

﴿It is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾ — that is, He made you a nation succeeding those before it. Qatada said: successors after successors, generation after generation. The khalf (successor) is the one who follows the one who preceded. It was said: He made you His vicegerents on His earth. So whoever among you disbelieves, his disbelief is upon him — that is, the harm of his disbelief is upon him, it does not go beyond him to others, and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them with their Lord except in hatred — that is, anger and enmity — and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss — that is, deficiency and destruction. The meaning is: disbelief does not benefit with God, since it increases them only in hatred, and it does not benefit them in themselves, since it increases them only in loss.

Then He (glory be to Him) commanded him to rebuke and confound them, saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered your partners, those you call upon besides God?﴾ — that is: tell me about the partners whom you took as gods and worshipped besides God. The clause "show me what they have created of the earth" is a substitutive clause of idtiyal (inclusive apposition) for "have you considered"; the meaning: tell me about your partners, show me what thing they created from the earth? It was said: the two verbs, "have you considered" and "show me," are from the construction of tanazu' (competition). The second has been made to govern, which is the preference of the Basrans. ﴿Or do they have a partnership in the heavens?﴾ — that is: do they have a share with God in creating them, or owning them, or disposing of them, so that by that they deserve a share in divinity? ﴿Or have We given them a Book?﴾ — that is: have We sent down to them a Book with partnership, so that they have ﴿clear proof﴾ from it — that is, a manifest, evident proof from that Book.

Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, and Hafs from ʿAsim read "bayyinatin" (singular), and the rest read it in the plural.

Muqatil said: he says, have We given the disbelievers of Makkah a Book, so that they have a clear statement from it that with God there is a partner?

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ) (marfu'an), something similar.

Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "The life span with which Allah rebuked them is sixty years."

al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Hakim, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lifespans of my community are between sixty and seventy, and few of them exceed that."

al-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: "Hasan gharib (a hadith that is fair in chain, but singular), which we do not know except through this route." Then he narrated it in another place in the Book of Asceticism (al-Zuhd) and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from the hadith of Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah, and it has been narrated through more than one route from him."

(p-١٢١٧) Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse that he said: "It is forty-six years."

Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, that he said: "The life span in which Allah left no excuse for the son of Adam by His saying ﴿Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein?﴾ is forty years."

Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Daraqutni in al-Afrad, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, and al-Khatib in his History narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say on the pulpit: "It occurred to the soul of Musa: Does Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sleep? So Allah sent to him an angel, who kept him awake for three nights, and gave him two flasks, one in each hand, and commanded him to guard them. He began to sleep, and his hands almost met, then he would wake and hold one back over the other, until he slept a single sleep, and his hands jerked and the two flasks broke." He said: "Allah struck for him a parable: if Allah, Blessed and Exalted, were to sleep, the heavens and the earth would not remain held together."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Salam that Musa said: "O Jibril, does your Lord sleep?" and he mentioned something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from his father, that Musa (said), and he mentioned something similar.

al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim (who authenticated it) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Indeed, the dung beetle is almost punished in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature﴾ (the verse).

Then, after He (glory be to Him) had finished speaking of the reward of His righteous servants, He mentioned the recompense of His wicked servants, saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell. They will not be decreed a death so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them.﴾ That is, no decree of death will be issued against them so that they might die and be at rest from the punishment. ﴿Nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾ — rather, ﴿every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment﴾ [an-Nisa: 56]. This verse is like His (glory be to Him) saying: ﴿Neither will he die therein nor live﴾ [Ta-Ha: 74]. The majority of readers read "fa-yamutu" (so that they die) in the accusative, as a response to the negation. ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar and al-Hasan read it with the nun retained (fa-yamutuna).

Al-Mazini said: it is in conjunction with "yuqda" (be decreed).

Ibn ʿAtiyya said: it is a weak reading, and there is no basis for this weakening; rather it is like His saying: ﴿nor will they be permitted, so that they may make excuses﴾ [al-Mursalat: 36]. ﴿Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ — that is, like that dreadful recompense, We recompense everyone who is extreme in disbelief. Abu ʿAmr read "yujza" in the passive voice.

﴿And they will cry out therein﴾ — from as-sarakh (al-sarakh), which is shouting, that is: they will call for help in the Fire, raising their voices. As-sarikh (al-sarikh) is the one who seeks help, and from this is the saying of the poet:

"When a frightened crier came to us, the shouting was for him a beating of the tambourine-skins."

﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteous deeds, other than what we used to do﴾ — that is, while they are therein crying out, they say: "Our Lord, etc."

Muqatil said: it is that they call out: "Our Lord, bring us out, we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do," from shirk and sins, so that we make faith in place of what we were upon of disbelief, and obedience in place of disobedience. The accusative of "salihan" is because it is an adjective of a deleted verbal noun, i.e., a righteous deed, or an adjective of a deleted noun, i.e., we will do something righteous.

It has been said: the addition of "other than what we used to do" is for regret over what they did of non-righteous deeds, along with their admission that their deeds in the world were not righteous. So God (glory be to Him) answers them with His saying: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would take heed might take heed therein?﴾ The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach, and the waw is for conjunction with an assumed element, as in its similar cases. "Ma" is an indefinite qualified noun, i.e., Did We not give you a lifespan in which whoever would be mindful could be mindful?

It was said: it is sixty years. It was said: forty. It was said: eighteen years. A group of the Companions said the first, al-Hasan and Masruq and others the second, and ʿAta' and Qatada the third.

al-Aʿmash read "ma yadhdhakkaru" with idgham (assimilation). ﴿And the warner came to you﴾. al-Wahidi said: most of the exegetes said: he is the Prophet (ﷺ).

ʿIkrima, Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna, Waki', al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl, al-Farra', and Ibn Jarir said: he is white hair (ash-shayb), and the meaning on this view is: Did We not give you life until you grew gray? It was said: he is the Qur'an. It was said: fever.

al-Azhari said: its meaning is that fever is the messenger of death, as it were, it signals its arrival and warns of its coming. White hair is also a warner, because it comes at the age of middle years, and it is a sign of leaving the age of youth, which is the age of play and amusement. It was said: he is the death of family and relatives. It was said: he is the perfection of intellect. It was said: puberty. ﴿So taste, for the wrongdoers have no helper﴾ — that is: taste the punishment of Hell, because you did not take heed and were not admonished; so you have no helper who would prevent you from the punishment of God or stand between you and it.

Muqatil said: "Taste the punishment; the polytheists have no preventer who would prevent them."

﴿Indeed, God knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾. The majority read "ʿalim" (knower) as idafa to "ghayb" (unseen). Jinah ibn Hubaysh read it with tanwin and the accusative "ghaybang" (ghaiban).

The meaning: He knows everything, and among that are deeds which are not hidden from Him; not one of them is concealed. So if He returned you to the world, you would not do righteous deeds, as He (glory be to Him) said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would revert to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾ — this is a justification of what precedes it, for when He knows the hidden thoughts within the breasts, which are the most hidden of all things, He knows what is above them a fortiori. It was said: this sentence explains the first sentence.

﴿It is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾ — that is, He made you a nation succeeding those before it. Qatada said: successors after successors, generation after generation. The khalf (successor) is the one who follows the one who preceded. It was said: He made you His vicegerents on His earth. So whoever among you disbelieves, his disbelief is upon him — that is, the harm of his disbelief is upon him, it does not go beyond him to others, and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them with their Lord except in hatred — that is, anger and enmity — and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss — that is, deficiency and destruction. The meaning is: disbelief does not benefit with God, since it increases them only in hatred, and it does not benefit them in themselves, since it increases them only in loss.

Then He (glory be to Him) commanded him to rebuke and confound them, saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered your partners, those you call upon besides God?﴾ — that is: tell me about the partners whom you took as gods and worshipped besides God. The clause "show me what they have created of the earth" is a substitutive clause of idtiyal (inclusive apposition) for "have you considered"; the meaning: tell me about your partners, show me what thing they created from the earth? It was said: the two verbs, "have you considered" and "show me," are from the construction of tanazu' (competition). The second has been made to govern, which is the preference of the Basrans. ﴿Or do they have a partnership in the heavens?﴾ — that is: do they have a share with God in creating them, or owning them, or disposing of them, so that by that they deserve a share in divinity? ﴿Or have We given them a Book?﴾ — that is: have We sent down to them a Book with partnership, so that they have ﴿clear proof﴾ from it — that is, a manifest, evident proof from that Book.

Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, and Hafs from ʿAsim read "bayyinatin" (singular), and the rest read it in the plural.

Muqatil said: he says, have We given the disbelievers of Makkah a Book, so that they have a clear statement from it that with God there is a partner?

Then He (glory be to Him) turned away from this to something else, saying: ﴿Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion﴾ — that is: what the wrongdoers promise one another, as their leaders and chiefs do with their followers in promises, is nothing but delusion, which they make appealing and adorn for them. It is the falsehoods which deceive and have no reality. That is their saying: these gods will benefit them, bring them near to God, and intercede for them with Him.

It was said: the devils promise the polytheists this. It was said: the meaning of the promise by which they promise one another is that they will be victorious over the Muslims and overcome them.

The clause ﴿Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease﴾ is a resumptive sentence explaining the power of God and the wondrous making of His handiwork, after explaining the weakness of the idols and their inability to do anything. It was said: the meaning is: their shirk requires the cessation of the heavens and the earth, as in His saying: ﴿The heavens are almost rent from above them, and the earth splits asunder, and the mountains fall in ruins, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son﴾ [Maryam: 90–91]. ﴿And if they should cease, none could hold them after Him﴾ — that is: none could hold them after His holding them, or after their cessation. The clause serves as the answer to the oath and the condition. The meaning of "lest they cease" is "so that they do not cease," or "lest they cease."

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that God prevents the heavens and the earth from ceasing, so there is no need for an assumed element.

al-Farra' said: that is, even if they ceased, none would hold them. He said: it is like His saying: ﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it yellowed, they would surely continue after it in disbelief﴾ [ar-Rum: 51]. It was said: the intended meaning is their cessation on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving﴾ — this is a justification of what precedes it, namely His holding the heavens and the earth.

﴿And they swore by God their most emphatic oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the nations﴾. The intended ones are Quraysh. They swore this oath before God sent Muhammad (ﷺ), when news reached them that the People of the Book had denied their messengers. The meaning of "than any one of the nations" is: the nations that denied the messengers. The warner is the Prophet, and "guidance" is uprightness. The Arabs used to wish that a messenger would come from among them as the messengers had come among the Children of Israel. When there came to them what they had wished for — and it was the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who is the noblest of warners and the most honorable of messengers, and was one of themselves — his coming only increased them in aversion from him and distance from answering him.

﴿Arrogance in the land﴾ — that is, because of arrogance and insolence. ﴿And evil scheming﴾ — that is, the evil scheming of deed, or they devised an evil scheme. Scheming is trickery, deception, and ugly action, and it is annexed to its attribute, as in His saying: "masjid al-jami'" (the congregational mosque) and "salat al-ula" (the first prayer). He made "ihda" (one of) feminine because "umma" (nation) is feminine, as al-Akhfash said.

It was said: the meaning is "one of the nations" in general. It was said: it is from the nation which is said to be "one of the nations," as a preference for it.

The majority read "wa-makra as-sayyi'" with the hamza of "as-sayyi'" in the genitive. al-A'mash and Hamza read it with sukun in pause (connected reading).

Many grammarians considered this reading erroneous, and they absolved al-A'mash, despite his eminence, of reading thus. They said: he used to pause with sukun, so whoever related from him that he read with sukun in connected speech made a mistake. The grammatical justification for this reading is possible: whoever reads it thus treats the connected reading as if it were a pause, as in the poet's saying:

"So today I drink, not bearing sin from God, nor being a lewd one."

with sukun on the ba' of "ashrab." A similar case is the reading of whoever reads "wa-ma yush'irkum" [al-An'am: 109] with sukun on the ra', and similarly Abu ʿAmr's reading "ila bari'kum" [al-Baqarah: 54] with sukun on the hamza, and there are many other examples.

Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: this is treating the connected reading as if it were a pause. Ibn Mas'ud read "wa-makran sayyi'an" (and an evil scheme). ﴿And the evil scheme does not encompass except its own people﴾ — that is, the consequence of evil descends only upon the one who committed evil.

al-Kalbi said: "yahiq" means "yuhit" (encompasses), and "al-hawq" is encompassing; it is said: "haqa bihi kadha" when it surrounded him. This is the apparent meaning of "yahiq" in the language of the Arabs. But Qutrub interpreted it here as "yanzil" (descends), and recited:

"They raised death, and it became light, a cubit after it had been enveloping."

That is: it descends. ﴿So do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?﴾ — that is: do they await anything but the way of the former peoples, that is: God's way concerning them, that the punishment descend upon these as it descended upon those. ﴿So you will not find any alteration in the way of God﴾ — that is: no one is able to change God's way which He established for the denying nations by sending down His punishment upon them, by placing something else in its place instead. ﴿And you will not find any transformation in the way of God﴾ — that is: that He would transform what the way of God has ordained of punishment, so that He would avert it from them and place it upon others. The negation of finding alteration and transformation is an expression for the negation of their existence.

﴿Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ This sentence is brought to establish and confirm the meaning of what precedes it — that is: have they not traveled through the land and seen what We sent down upon 'Ad, Thamud, Madyan, and their likes of punishment when they denied the messengers? For that is of God's way with the deniers, which is neither altered nor transformed. The traces of their punishment and what God sent upon them remain in their dwellings, manifest in their places. And the situation is that those were stronger than these in power, longer in life, greater in wealth, and mightier in bodies. ﴿And never would God be incapable of anything in the heavens or on the earth﴾ — that is: it is not for Him to be outstripped or escaped by anything among things, whatever it may be, in them. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Knowing, Competent﴾ — that is: abundant in knowledge and abundant in power, nothing is hidden from Him and no matter is difficult for Him.

﴿And if God were to seize mankind for what they have earned﴾ — of sins — and for what they have done of wrongdoings, ﴿He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature that moves﴾ — whatever it may be. As for the children of Adam, it is because of their sins; and as for others, it is because of the ill omen of the disobedience of the children of Adam.

And it was said: the intended meaning is that He left on the surface of the earth no moving creature (dabbah) of the children of Adam or the jinn. Ibn Mas'ud and Qatadah held the first view, and al-Kalbi held the second.

Ibn Jurayj, al-Akhfash, and al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: by "dabbah" here they meant only humans, not others, but He delays them until a specified term, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever Seer of His servants﴾, that is, of those among them who deserve reward and of those who deserve punishment. The governing element (al-'amil) of "idha" (when) is "jaa'" (comes), not "basiran" (Seer). In this there is consolation for the believers and a warning to the disbelievers.

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein?﴾, that he said: "Sixty years."

Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated from him that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: Where are the sons of sixty? This is the age of which Allah said: ﴿Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein?﴾" In its chain is Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl al-Makhzumi, and there is some criticism of him.

Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has left no excuse for a man whose life He extended until he reached sixty years."

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ) (marfu'an), something similar.

Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "The life span with which Allah rebuked them is sixty years."

The clause "show me what they have created of the earth" is a substitutive clause of idtiyal (inclusive apposition) for "have you considered"; the meaning: tell me about your partners, show me what thing they created from the earth? The second has been made to govern, which is the preference of the Basrans. ﴿Or do they have a partnership in the heavens?﴾ — that is: do they have a share with God in creating them, or owning them, or disposing of them, so that by that they deserve a share in divinity? ﴿Or have We given them a Book?﴾ — that is: have We sent down to them a Book with partnership, so that they have ﴿clear proof﴾ from it — that is, a manifest, evident proof from that Book.

Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, and Hafs from ʿAsim read "bayyinatin" (singular), and the rest read it in the plural.

Muqatil said: he says, have We given the disbelievers of Makkah a Book, so that they have a clear statement from it that with God there is a partner?

Then He (glory be to Him) turned away from this to something else, saying: ﴿Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion﴾ — that is: what the wrongdoers promise one another, as their leaders and chiefs do with their followers in promises, is nothing but delusion, which they make appealing and adorn for them. It is the falsehoods which deceive and have no reality. That is their saying: these gods will benefit them, bring them near to God, and intercede for them with Him.

It was said: the devils promise the polytheists this. It was said: the meaning of the promise by which they promise one another is that they will be victorious over the Muslims and overcome them.

The clause ﴿Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease﴾ is a resumptive sentence explaining the power of God and the wondrous making of His handiwork, after explaining the weakness of the idols and their inability to do anything. It was said: the meaning is: their shirk requires the cessation of the heavens and the earth, as in His saying: ﴿The heavens are almost rent from above them, and the earth splits asunder, and the mountains fall in ruins, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son﴾ [Maryam: 90–91]. ﴿And if they should cease, none could hold them after Him﴾ — that is: none could hold them after His holding them, or after their cessation. The clause serves as the answer to the oath and the condition. The meaning of "lest they cease" is "so that they do not cease," or "lest they cease."

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that God prevents the heavens and the earth from ceasing, so there is no need for an assumed element.

al-Farra' said: that is, even if they ceased, none would hold them. He said: it is like His saying: ﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it yellowed, they would surely continue after it in disbelief﴾ [ar-Rum: 51]. It was said: the intended meaning is their cessation on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving﴾ — this is a justification of what precedes it, namely His holding the heavens and the earth.

﴿And they swore by God their most emphatic oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the nations﴾. The intended ones are Quraysh. They swore this oath before God sent Muhammad (ﷺ), when news reached them that the People of the Book had denied their messengers. The meaning of "than any one of the nations" is: the nations that denied the messengers. The warner is the Prophet, and "guidance" is uprightness. The Arabs used to wish that a messenger would come from among them as the messengers had come among the Children of Israel. When there came to them what they had wished for — and it was the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who is the noblest of warners and the most honorable of messengers, and was one of themselves — his coming only increased them in aversion from him and distance from answering him.

﴿Arrogance in the land﴾ — that is, because of arrogance and insolence. ﴿And evil scheming﴾ — that is, the evil scheming of deed, or they devised an evil scheme. Scheming is trickery, deception, and ugly action, and it is annexed to its attribute, as in His saying: "masjid al-jami'" (the congregational mosque) and "salat al-ula" (the first prayer). He made "ihda" (one of) feminine because "umma" (nation) is feminine, as al-Akhfash said.

It was said: the meaning is "one of the nations" in general. It was said: it is from the nation which is said to be "one of the nations," as a preference for it.

The majority read "wa-makra as-sayyi'" with the hamza of "as-sayyi'" in the genitive. al-A'mash and Hamza read it with sukun in pause (connected reading).

Many grammarians considered this reading erroneous, and they absolved al-A'mash, despite his eminence, of reading thus. They said: he used to pause with sukun, so whoever related from him that he read with sukun in connected speech made a mistake. The grammatical justification for this reading is possible: whoever reads it thus treats the connected reading as if it were a pause, as in the poet's saying:

"So today I drink, not bearing sin from God, nor being a lewd one."

with sukun on the ba' of "ashrab." A similar case is the reading of whoever reads "wa-ma yush'irkum" [al-An'am: 109] with sukun on the ra', and similarly Abu ʿAmr's reading "ila bari'kum" [al-Baqarah: 54] with sukun on the hamza, and there are many other examples.

Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: this is treating the connected reading as if it were a pause. Ibn Mas'ud read "wa-makran sayyi'an" (and an evil scheme). ﴿And the evil scheme does not encompass except its own people﴾ — that is, the consequence of evil descends only upon the one who committed evil.

al-Kalbi said: "yahiq" means "yuhit" (encompasses), and "al-hawq" is encompassing; it is said: "haqa bihi kadha" when it surrounded him. This is the apparent meaning of "yahiq" in the language of the Arabs. But Qutrub interpreted it here as "yanzil" (descends), and recited:

"They raised death, and it became light, a cubit after it had been enveloping."

That is: it descends. ﴿So do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?﴾ — that is: do they await anything but the way of the former peoples, that is: God's way concerning them, that the punishment descend upon these as it descended upon those. ﴿So you will not find any alteration in the way of God﴾ — that is: no one is able to change God's way which He established for the denying nations by sending down His punishment upon them, by placing something else in its place instead. ﴿And you will not find any transformation in the way of God﴾ — that is: that He would transform what the way of God has ordained of punishment, so that He would avert it from them and place it upon others. The negation of finding alteration and transformation is an expression for the negation of their existence.

﴿Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ This sentence is brought to establish and confirm the meaning of what precedes it — that is: have they not traveled through the land and seen what We sent down upon 'Ad, Thamud, Madyan, and their likes of punishment when they denied the messengers? For that is of God's way with the deniers, which is neither altered nor transformed. The traces of their punishment and what God sent upon them remain in their dwellings, manifest in their places. And the situation is that those were stronger than these in power, longer in life, greater in wealth, and mightier in bodies. ﴿And never would God be incapable of anything in the heavens or on the earth﴾ — that is: it is not for Him to be outstripped or escaped by anything among things, whatever it may be, in them. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Knowing, Competent﴾ — that is: abundant in knowledge and abundant in power, nothing is hidden from Him and no matter is difficult for Him.

﴿And if God were to seize mankind for what they have earned﴾ — of sins — and for what they have done of wrongdoings, ﴿He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature that moves﴾ — whatever it may be. As for the children of Adam, it is because of their sins; and as for others, it is because of the ill omen of the disobedience of the children of Adam.

And it was said: the intended meaning is that He left on the surface of the earth no moving creature (dabbah) of the children of Adam or the jinn. Ibn Mas'ud and Qatadah held the first view, and al-Kalbi held the second.

Ibn Jurayj, al-Akhfash, and al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: by "dabbah" here they meant only humans, not others, but He delays them until a specified term, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever Seer of His servants﴾, that is, of those among them who deserve reward and of those who deserve punishment. The governing element (al-'amil) of "idha" (when) is "jaa'" (comes), not "basiran" (Seer). In this there is consolation for the believers and a warning to the disbelievers.

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein?﴾, that he said: "Sixty years."

Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated from him that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: Where are the sons of sixty? This is the age of which Allah said: ﴿Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein?﴾" In its chain is Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl al-Makhzumi, and there is some criticism of him.

Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has left no excuse for a man whose life He extended until he reached sixty years."

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ) (marfu'an), something similar.

Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "The life span with which Allah rebuked them is sixty years."

al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Hakim, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lifespans of my community are between sixty and seventy, and few of them exceed that."

al-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: "Hasan gharib (a hadith that is fair in chain, but singular), which we do not know except through this route." Then he narrated it in another place in the Book of Asceticism (al-Zuhd) and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from the hadith of Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah, and it has been narrated through more than one route from him."

(p-١٢١٧) Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse that he said: "It is forty-six years."

Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, that he said: "The life span in which Allah left no excuse for the son of Adam by His saying ﴿Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein?﴾ is forty years."

Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Daraqutni in al-Afrad, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, and al-Khatib in his History narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say on the pulpit: "It occurred to the soul of Musa: Does Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sleep? So Allah sent to him an angel, who kept him awake for three nights, and gave him two flasks, one in each hand, and commanded him to guard them. He began to sleep, and his hands almost met, then he would wake and hold one back over the other, until he slept a single sleep, and his hands jerked and the two flasks broke." He said: "Allah struck for him a parable: if Allah, Blessed and Exalted, were to sleep, the heavens and the earth would not remain held together."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Salam that Musa said: "O Jibril, does your Lord sleep?" and he mentioned something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from his father, that Musa (said), and he mentioned something similar.

al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim (who authenticated it) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Indeed, the dung beetle is almost punished in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature﴾ (the verse).

Then, after He (glory be to Him) had finished speaking of the reward of His righteous servants, He mentioned the recompense of His wicked servants, saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell. They will not be decreed a death so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them.﴾ That is, no decree of death will be issued against them so that they might die and be at rest from the punishment. ﴿Nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾ — rather, ﴿every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment﴾ [an-Nisa: 56]. This verse is like His (glory be to Him) saying: ﴿Neither will he die therein nor live﴾ [Ta-Ha: 74]. The majority of readers read "fa-yamutu" (so that they die) in the accusative, as a response to the negation. ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar and al-Hasan read it with the nun retained (fa-yamutuna).

Al-Mazini said: it is in conjunction with "yuqda" (be decreed).

Ibn ʿAtiyya said: it is a weak reading, and there is no basis for this weakening; rather it is like His saying: ﴿nor will they be permitted, so that they may make excuses﴾ [al-Mursalat: 36]. ﴿Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ — that is, like that dreadful recompense, We recompense everyone who is extreme in disbelief. Abu ʿAmr read "yujza" in the passive voice.

﴿And they will cry out therein﴾ — from as-sarakh (al-sarakh), which is shouting, that is: they will call for help in the Fire, raising their voices. As-sarikh (al-sarikh) is the one who seeks help, and from this is the saying of the poet:

"When a frightened crier came to us, the shouting was for him a beating of the tambourine-skins."

﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteous deeds, other than what we used to do﴾ — that is, while they are therein crying out, they say: "Our Lord, etc."

Muqatil said: it is that they call out: "Our Lord, bring us out, we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do," from shirk and sins, so that we make faith in place of what we were upon of disbelief, and obedience in place of disobedience. The accusative of "salihan" is because it is an adjective of a deleted verbal noun, i.e., a righteous deed, or an adjective of a deleted noun, i.e., we will do something righteous.

It has been said: the addition of "other than what we used to do" is for regret over what they did of non-righteous deeds, along with their admission that their deeds in the world were not righteous. So God (glory be to Him) answers them with His saying: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would take heed might take heed therein?﴾ The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach, and the waw is for conjunction with an assumed element, as in its similar cases. "Ma" is an indefinite qualified noun, i.e., Did We not give you a lifespan in which whoever would be mindful could be mindful?

It was said: it is sixty years. It was said: forty. It was said: eighteen years. A group of the Companions said the first, al-Hasan and Masruq and others the second, and ʿAta' and Qatada the third.

al-Aʿmash read "ma yadhdhakkaru" with idgham (assimilation). ﴿And the warner came to you﴾. al-Wahidi said: most of the exegetes said: he is the Prophet (ﷺ).

ʿIkrima, Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna, Waki', al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl, al-Farra', and Ibn Jarir said: he is white hair (ash-shayb), and the meaning on this view is: Did We not give you life until you grew gray? It was said: he is the Qur'an. It was said: fever.

al-Azhari said: its meaning is that fever is the messenger of death, as it were, it signals its arrival and warns of its coming. White hair is also a warner, because it comes at the age of middle years, and it is a sign of leaving the age of youth, which is the age of play and amusement. It was said: he is the death of family and relatives. It was said: he is the perfection of intellect. It was said: puberty. ﴿So taste, for the wrongdoers have no helper﴾ — that is: taste the punishment of Hell, because you did not take heed and were not admonished; so you have no helper who would prevent you from the punishment of God or stand between you and it.

Muqatil said: "Taste the punishment; the polytheists have no preventer who would prevent them."

﴿Indeed, God knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾. The majority read "ʿalim" (knower) as idafa to "ghayb" (unseen). Jinah ibn Hubaysh read it with tanwin and the accusative "ghaybang" (ghaiban).

The meaning: He knows everything, and among that are deeds which are not hidden from Him; not one of them is concealed. So if He returned you to the world, you would not do righteous deeds, as He (glory be to Him) said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would revert to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾ — this is a justification of what precedes it, for when He knows the hidden thoughts within the breasts, which are the most hidden of all things, He knows what is above them a fortiori. It was said: this sentence explains the first sentence.

﴿It is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾ — that is, He made you a nation succeeding those before it. Qatada said: successors after successors, generation after generation. The khalf (successor) is the one who follows the one who preceded. It was said: He made you His vicegerents on His earth. So whoever among you disbelieves, his disbelief is upon him — that is, the harm of his disbelief is upon him, it does not go beyond him to others, and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them with their Lord except in hatred — that is, anger and enmity — and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss — that is, deficiency and destruction. The meaning is: disbelief does not benefit with God, since it increases them only in hatred, and it does not benefit them in themselves, since it increases them only in loss.

Then He (glory be to Him) commanded him to rebuke and confound them, saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered your partners, those you call upon besides God?﴾ — that is: tell me about the partners whom you took as gods and worshipped besides God. Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated from him that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: Where are the sons of sixty? Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has left no excuse for a man whose life He extended until he reached sixty years."

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ) (marfu'an), something similar.

Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "The life span with which Allah rebuked them is sixty years."

al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Hakim, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lifespans of my community are between sixty and seventy, and few of them exceed that."

al-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: "Hasan gharib (a hadith that is fair in chain, but singular), which we do not know except through this route." Then he narrated it in another place in the Book of Asceticism (al-Zuhd) and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from the hadith of Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah, and it has been narrated through more than one route from him."

(p-١٢١٧) Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse that he said: "It is forty-six years."

Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, that he said: "The life span in which Allah left no excuse for the son of Adam by His saying ﴿Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein?﴾ is forty years."

Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Daraqutni in al-Afrad, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, and al-Khatib in his History narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say on the pulpit: "It occurred to the soul of Musa: Does Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sleep? So Allah sent to him an angel, who kept him awake for three nights, and gave him two flasks, one in each hand, and commanded him to guard them. He began to sleep, and his hands almost met, then he would wake and hold one back over the other, until he slept a single sleep, and his hands jerked and the two flasks broke." He said: "Allah struck for him a parable: if Allah, Blessed and Exalted, were to sleep, the heavens and the earth would not remain held together."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Salam that Musa said: "O Jibril, does your Lord sleep?" and he mentioned something similar.

Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from his father, that Musa (said), and he mentioned something similar.

al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim (who authenticated it) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Indeed, the dung beetle is almost punished in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature﴾ (the verse).

Then, after He (glory be to Him) had finished speaking of the reward of His righteous servants, He mentioned the recompense of His wicked servants, saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell. They will not be decreed a death so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them.﴾ That is, no decree of death will be issued against them so that they might die and be at rest from the punishment. ﴿Nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾ — rather, ﴿every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment﴾ [an-Nisa: 56]. This verse is like His (glory be to Him) saying: ﴿Neither will he die therein nor live﴾ [Ta-Ha: 74]. The majority of readers read "fa-yamutu" (so that they die) in the accusative, as a response to the negation. ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar and al-Hasan read it with the nun retained (fa-yamutuna).

Al-Mazini said: it is in conjunction with "yuqda" (be decreed).

Ibn ʿAtiyya said: it is a weak reading, and there is no basis for this weakening; rather it is like His saying: ﴿nor will they be permitted, so that they may make excuses﴾ [al-Mursalat: 36]. ﴿Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ — that is, like that dreadful recompense, We recompense everyone who is extreme in disbelief. Abu ʿAmr read "yujza" in the passive voice.

﴿And they will cry out therein﴾ — from as-sarakh (al-sarakh), which is shouting, that is: they will call for help in the Fire, raising their voices. As-sarikh (al-sarikh) is the one who seeks help, and from this is the saying of the poet:

"When a frightened crier came to us, the shouting was for him a beating of the tambourine-skins."

﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteous deeds, other than what we used to do﴾ — that is, while they are therein crying out, they say: "Our Lord, etc."

Muqatil said: it is that they call out: "Our Lord, bring us out, we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do," from shirk and sins, so that we make faith in place of what we were upon of disbelief, and obedience in place of disobedience. The accusative of "salihan" is because it is an adjective of a deleted verbal noun, i.e., a righteous deed, or an adjective of a deleted noun, i.e., we will do something righteous.

It has been said: the addition of "other than what we used to do" is for regret over what they did of non-righteous deeds, along with their admission that their deeds in the world were not righteous. So God (glory be to Him) answers them with His saying: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would take heed might take heed therein?﴾ The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach, and the waw is for conjunction with an assumed element, as in its similar cases. "Ma" is an indefinite qualified noun, i.e., Did We not give you a lifespan in which whoever would be mindful could be mindful?

It was said: it is sixty years. It was said: forty. It was said: eighteen years. A group of the Companions said the first, al-Hasan and Masruq and others the second, and ʿAta' and Qatada the third.

al-Aʿmash read "ma yadhdhakkaru" with idgham (assimilation). ﴿And the warner came to you﴾. al-Wahidi said: most of the exegetes said: he is the Prophet (ﷺ).

ʿIkrima, Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna, Waki', al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl, al-Farra', and Ibn Jarir said: he is white hair (ash-shayb), and the meaning on this view is: Did We not give you life until you grew gray? It was said: he is the Qur'an. It was said: fever.

al-Azhari said: its meaning is that fever is the messenger of death, as it were, it signals its arrival and warns of its coming. White hair is also a warner, because it comes at the age of middle years, and it is a sign of leaving the age of youth, which is the age of play and amusement. It was said: he is the death of family and relatives. It was said: he is the perfection of intellect. It was said: puberty. ﴿So taste, for the wrongdoers have no helper﴾ — that is: taste the punishment of Hell, because you did not take heed and were not admonished; so you have no helper who would prevent you from the punishment of God or stand between you and it.

Muqatil said: "Taste the punishment; the polytheists have no preventer who would prevent them."

﴿Indeed, God knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾. The majority read "ʿalim" (knower) as idafa to "ghayb" (unseen). Jinah ibn Hubaysh read it with tanwin and the accusative "ghaybang" (ghaiban).

The meaning: He knows everything, and among that are deeds which are not hidden from Him; not one of them is concealed. So if He returned you to the world, you would not do righteous deeds, as He (glory be to Him) said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would revert to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾ — this is a justification of what precedes it, for when He knows the hidden thoughts within the breasts, which are the most hidden of all things, He knows what is above them a fortiori. It was said: this sentence explains the first sentence.

﴿It is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾ — that is, He made you a nation succeeding those before it. Qatada said: successors after successors, generation after generation. The khalf (successor) is the one who follows the one who preceded. It was said: He made you His vicegerents on His earth. So whoever among you disbelieves, his disbelief is upon him — that is, the harm of his disbelief is upon him, it does not go beyond him to others, and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them with their Lord except in hatred — that is, anger and enmity — and the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss — that is, deficiency and destruction. The meaning is: disbelief does not benefit with God, since it increases them only in hatred, and it does not benefit them in themselves, since it increases them only in loss.

Then He (glory be to Him) commanded him to rebuke and confound them, saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered your partners, those you call upon besides God?﴾ — that is: tell me about the partners whom you took as gods and worshipped besides God. The clause "show me what they have created of the earth" is a substitutive clause of idtiyal (inclusive apposition) for "have you considered"; the meaning: tell me about your partners, show me what thing they created from the earth? It was said: the two verbs, "have you considered" and "show me," are from the construction of tanazu' (competition). The second has been made to govern, which is the preference of the Basrans. ﴿Or do they have a partnership in the heavens?﴾ — that is: do they have a share with God in creating them, or owning them, or disposing of them, so that by that they deserve a share in divinity? ﴿Or have We given them a Book?﴾ — that is: have We sent down to them a Book with partnership, so that they have ﴿clear proof﴾ from it — that is, a manifest, evident proof from that Book.

Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, and Hafs from ʿAsim read "bayyinatin" (singular), and the rest read it in the plural.

Muqatil said: he says, have We given the disbelievers of Makkah a Book, so that they have a clear statement from it that with God there is a partner?

Then He (glory be to Him) turned away from this to something else, saying: ﴿Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion﴾ — that is: what the wrongdoers promise one another, as their leaders and chiefs do with their followers in promises, is nothing but delusion, which they make appealing and adorn for them. It is the falsehoods which deceive and have no reality. That is their saying: these gods will benefit them, bring them near to God, and intercede for them with Him.

It was said: the devils promise the polytheists this. It was said: the meaning of the promise by which they promise one another is that they will be victorious over the Muslims and overcome them.

The clause ﴿Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease﴾ is a resumptive sentence explaining the power of God and the wondrous making of His handiwork, after explaining the weakness of the idols and their inability to do anything. It was said: the meaning is: their shirk requires the cessation of the heavens and the earth, as in His saying: ﴿The heavens are almost rent from above them, and the earth splits asunder, and the mountains fall in ruins, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son﴾ [Maryam: 90–91]. ﴿And if they should cease, none could hold them after Him﴾ — that is: none could hold them after His holding them, or after their cessation. The clause serves as the answer to the oath and the condition. The meaning of "lest they cease" is "so that they do not cease," or "lest they cease."

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that God prevents the heavens and the earth from ceasing, so there is no need for an assumed element.

al-Farra' said: that is, even if they ceased, none would hold them. He said: it is like His saying: ﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it yellowed, they would surely continue after it in disbelief﴾ [ar-Rum: 51]. It was said: the intended meaning is their cessation on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving﴾ — this is a justification of what precedes it, namely His holding the heavens and the earth.

﴿And they swore by God their most emphatic oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the nations﴾. The intended ones are Quraysh. They swore this oath before God sent Muhammad (ﷺ), when news reached them that the People of the Book had denied their messengers. The meaning of "than any one of the nations" is: the nations that denied the messengers. The warner is the Prophet, and "guidance" is uprightness. The Arabs used to wish that a messenger would come from among them as the messengers had come among the Children of Israel. When there came to them what they had wished for — and it was the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who is the noblest of warners and the most honorable of messengers, and was one of themselves — his coming only increased them in aversion from him and distance from answering him.

﴿Arrogance in the land﴾ — that is, because of arrogance and insolence. ﴿And evil scheming﴾ — that is, the evil scheming of deed, or they devised an evil scheme. Scheming is trickery, deception, and ugly action, and it is annexed to its attribute, as in His saying: "masjid al-jami'" (the congregational mosque) and "salat al-ula" (the first prayer). He made "ihda" (one of) feminine because "umma" (nation) is feminine, as al-Akhfash said.

It was said: the meaning is "one of the nations" in general. It was said: it is from the nation which is said to be "one of the nations," as a preference for it.

The majority read "wa-makra as-sayyi'" with the hamza of "as-sayyi'" in the genitive. al-A'mash and Hamza read it with sukun in pause (connected reading).

Many grammarians considered this reading erroneous, and they absolved al-A'mash, despite his eminence, of reading thus. They said: he used to pause with sukun, so whoever related from him that he read with sukun in connected speech made a mistake. The grammatical justification for this reading is possible: whoever reads it thus treats the connected reading as if it were a pause, as in the poet's saying:

"So today I drink, not bearing sin from God, nor being a lewd one."

with sukun on the ba' of "ashrab." A similar case is the reading of whoever reads "wa-ma yush'irkum" [al-An'am: 109] with sukun on the ra', and similarly Abu ʿAmr's reading "ila bari'kum" [al-Baqarah: 54] with sukun on the hamza, and there are many other examples.

Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: this is treating the connected reading as if it were a pause. Ibn Mas'ud read "wa-makran sayyi'an" (and an evil scheme). ﴿And the evil scheme does not encompass except its own people﴾ — that is, the consequence of evil descends only upon the one who committed evil.

al-Kalbi said: "yahiq" means "yuhit" (encompasses), and "al-hawq" is encompassing; it is said: "haqa bihi kadha" when it surrounded him. This is the apparent meaning of "yahiq" in the language of the Arabs. But Qutrub interpreted it here as "yanzil" (descends), and recited:

"They raised death, and it became light, a cubit after it had been enveloping."

That is: it descends. ﴿So do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?﴾ — that is: do they await anything but the way of the former peoples, that is: God's way concerning them, that the punishment descend upon these as it descended upon those. ﴿So you will not find any alteration in the way of God﴾ — that is: no one is able to change God's way which He established for the denying nations by sending down His punishment upon them, by placing something else in its place instead. ﴿And you will not find any transformation in the way of God﴾ — that is: that He would transform what the way of God has ordained of punishment, so that He would avert it from them and place it upon others. The negation of finding alteration and transformation is an expression for the negation of their existence.

﴿Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ This sentence is brought to establish and confirm the meaning of what precedes it — that is: have they not traveled through the land and seen what We sent down upon 'Ad, Thamud, Madyan, and their likes of punishment when they denied the messengers? For that is of God's way with the deniers, which is neither altered nor transformed. The traces of their punishment and what God sent upon them remain in their dwellings, manifest in their places. And the situation is that those were stronger than these in power, longer in life, greater in wealth, and mightier in bodies. ﴿And never would God be incapable of anything in the heavens or on the earth﴾ — that is: it is not for Him to be outstripped or escaped by anything among things, whatever it may be, in them. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Knowing, Competent﴾ — that is: abundant in knowledge and abundant in power, nothing is hidden from Him and no matter is difficult for Him.

﴿And if God were to seize mankind for what they have earned﴾ — of sins — and for what they have done of wrongdoings, ﴿He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature that moves﴾ — whatever it may be. As for the children of Adam, it is because of their sins; and as for others, it is because of the ill omen of the disobedience of the children of Adam.

And it was said: the intended meaning is that He left on the surface of the earth no moving creature (dabbah) of the children of Adam or the jinn. Ibn Mas'ud and Qatadah held the first view, and al-Kalbi held the second.

Ibn Jurayj, al-Akhfash, and al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: by "dabbah" here they meant only humans, not others, but He delays them until a specified term, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever Seer of His servants﴾, that is, of those among them who deserve reward and of those who deserve punishment. The governing element (al-'amil) of "idha" (when) is "jaa'" (comes), not "basiran" (Seer). In this there is consolation for the believers and a warning to the disbelievers.

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein?﴾, that he said: "Sixty years."
